case_title: Bikramjit Singh v. The State of Punjab
statutory_provisions: IPC s.302, s.307, s.452, s.427, s.341, s.34; Arms Act s.25; Explosive Substances Act ss.3,4,5,6; Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act ss.13, 16, 18, 18-B, 20
neutral_facts: The accused, a security guard, was involved in an incident where a hand grenade was thrown on the stage of a public gathering, resulting in 22 persons sustaining serious injuries, out of which 3 persons died. The accused was apprehended and remanded to custody. After 90 days in custody, an application for default bail was made, but it was dismissed on the grounds that the time for investigation had been extended to 180 days. The accused challenged this decision, and the Special Court set aside the order extending the time, holding that the Special Court alone had jurisdiction to extend the time. The charge sheet was filed after the accused's application for default bail. The High Court initially dismissed the application for default bail, but the Supreme Court set aside the High Court's judgment, holding that the accused was entitled to default bail under Section 167(2) of the Code of Criminal Procedure, as amended by Section 43-D of the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act.
